note: One pair of open chords per block, changed back and forth: Em and Am, then E and Am (one shape moved over a string), then A and D (one finger leads). Each block has one goal line; the fingering stays in the chord boxes. The key is the lesson, so there are no moves.

exercise.title: Changes, one pair at a time
exercise.why: A change gets quick when the fingers leave together and land together, and that comes from making one change many times in a row, so each block is one pair of chords and nothing else.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Change between Em and Am with one strum on each, then rest your hand and go again.
Practice until the change is in your muscle memory: all your fingers lift at once and land at once.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Change between E and Am the same way: the boxes show one shape in two places, so all three fingers move across one string together.
Practice until the shape holds while it moves.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Change between A and D the same way: one finger stays on the B string and slides up one fret, so let it lead and put the other two fingers down around it.
Go slowly enough that D is ready before you strum it.
